questions.question: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.fact: Spiders aren't insects: they're arachnids, like scorpions and ticks. Most spiders also have eight eyes.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.fact: Mars looks red because its dust is full of iron oxide, which is basically rust. It also has the tallest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons.

questions.question: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.fact: The Pacific is bigger than all of Earth's land put together, and it holds the deepest point on the planet, the Mariana Trench.

questions.question: What do bees make?
questions.fact: A honeybee makes only about a twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its whole life. Edible honey has been found in ancient Egyptian tombs.

questions.question: What is the hardest natural substance?
questions.fact: Diamonds are pure carbon, the same element as the graphite in pencils. The only difference is how the atoms are arranged.

questions.question: How many minutes are there in a day?
questions.fact: Earth actually takes about 23 hours and 56 minutes to spin once compared with the stars. The extra minutes come from its trip around the Sun.

questions.question: Which fruit wears its seeds on the outside?
questions.fact: An average strawberry has about 200 "seeds" on the outside. Botanically, each one is a tiny fruit of its own.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.fact: The symbol Au comes from "aurum", Latin for gold. All the gold ever mined would fit in a cube about 22 metres on each side.

questions.question: Which animal is called the "King of the Jungle"?
questions.fact: Despite the nickname, lions live mostly in savannas and grasslands, not jungles. A lion's roar can be heard up to 8 km away.

questions.question: How many players does a football (soccer) team have on the pitch?
questions.fact: The first international football match was played in 1872, between Scotland and England. It ended 0–0.

questions.question: What colour do you get when you mix blue and yellow?
questions.fact: Paint and light mix differently: blue and yellow paint make green, but red and green light make yellow.

questions.question: Pizza Margherita is named after a queen of which country?
questions.fact: Legend says the pizza was named for Queen Margherita of Savoy in 1889. Its red, white and green match the Italian flag.

questions.question: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.fact: A cheetah can reach about 100 km/h in around three seconds, but it can only sprint for about 30 seconds before it overheats.

questions.question: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.fact: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood. Two hearts pump blood through the gills and the third pumps it round the body.

questions.question: Which instrument usually has 88 keys?
questions.fact: A standard piano has 52 white keys and 36 black keys. It was invented in Italy around 1700 by Bartolomeo Cristofori.

questions.question: On which date is Valentine's Day celebrated?
questions.fact: Valentine's Day is named after a Christian martyr, Saint Valentine. Sending Valentine's cards became popular in the 1800s.

questions.question: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
questions.fact: Mandarin has about a billion native speakers. It is tonal: the same syllable can mean different things depending on the pitch.

questions.question: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.fact: More than 1,300 Earths could fit inside Jupiter, and its Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than our whole planet.

questions.question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.fact: The Mona Lisa was stolen from the Louvre in 1911 and missing for two years before it turned up in Florence.

questions.question: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.fact: Bees build honeycomb in hexagons because that shape stores the most honey using the least wax.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient in guacamole?
questions.fact: Avocados are botanically berries with one big seed. The word "guacamole" comes from Nahuatl, the Aztec language.

questions.question: Which gas do plants take in from the air to make food?
questions.fact: A large tree can take in around 20 kg of carbon dioxide a year and release the oxygen we breathe.

questions.question: How many is a "baker's dozen"?
questions.fact: The "baker's dozen" is said to come from medieval bakers adding a 13th loaf so nobody could accuse them of selling short.

questions.question: Which bird is a worldwide symbol of peace?
questions.fact: The dove with an olive branch comes from the story of Noah's Ark. Picasso drew a famous peace dove in 1949.

questions.question: In which year did a person first walk on the Moon?
questions.fact: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on 20 July 1969. With no wind on the Moon, the astronauts' footprints are probably still there.

questions.question: In Spain, what do people traditionally eat at midnight on New Year's Eve?
questions.fact: One grape goes with each of the 12 chimes of midnight, for 12 lucky months. The tradition took off in the early 1900s.

questions.question: Which famous puzzle cube was invented in Hungary in 1974?
questions.fact: Ernő Rubik made the cube as a teaching tool and needed about a month to solve it himself. Top speedcubers now do it in about 3 seconds.

questions.question: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
questions.fact: A standard guitar is tuned E, A, D, G, B, E. The modern classical guitar shape was developed in Spain by Antonio de Torres in the 1800s.

questions.question: Which vitamin does your skin make when it gets sunlight?
questions.fact: Your skin makes vitamin D from UVB sunlight. It helps your body absorb calcium for strong bones.

questions.question: What is the tallest animal in the world?
questions.fact: A giraffe's neck has seven bones, the same number as a human neck. Each one is just much longer.

questions.question: How many days are there in a leap year?
questions.fact: Leap years exist because Earth takes about 365 and a quarter days to go round the Sun. People born on 29 February are called "leaplings".

questions.question: How many hours are there in a week?
questions.fact: There are 168 hours in a week, and the average person sleeps about a third of them.

questions.question: What is the square root of 144?
questions.fact: 144 is a dozen dozens, also called a gross. It is also the 12th number in the Fibonacci sequence.

questions.question: What is 15% of 200?
questions.fact: Quick trick: 10% of 200 is 20 and 5% is half that, 10. Add them together and 15% is 30.

questions.question: Which month has the fewest days?
questions.fact: February has 28 days, or 29 in a leap year. January and February were added to the Roman calendar later than the other months.

questions.question: What is the Roman numeral for 10?
questions.fact: There is no zero in Roman numerals. The Romans had no symbol for it.

questions.question: What is the Roman numeral for 50?
questions.fact: L is 50, C is 100, D is 500 and M is 1,000. So 2026 is written MMXXVI.

questions.question: What is a shape with eight sides called?
questions.fact: Stop signs in most countries are octagons, so drivers can recognise them by shape alone, even when covered in snow.

questions.question: How many zeros are in one million?
questions.fact: If you counted one number every second, non-stop, it would take about 11 and a half days to reach a million.

questions.question: What is a baby cat called?
questions.fact: Kittens are born with their eyes closed and open them at about one to two weeks old. A group of kittens is called a "kindle".

questions.question: What colour do you get by mixing red and yellow?
questions.fact: The colour orange was named after the fruit, not the other way round. Before that, English speakers called it "yellow-red".

questions.question: What is the opposite direction of north-east?
questions.fact: South-west is directly opposite north-east. Traditional compass roses show 32 points.

questions.question: Which is the coldest continent?
questions.fact: Antarctica is the coldest, windiest and driest continent. Its record low is about −89 °C.

questions.question: What is the tallest mountain in the world?
questions.fact: Everest is about 8,849 metres high and still grows a few millimetres a year as India keeps pushing into Asia.

questions.question: Which is the largest country in South America?
questions.fact: Brazil covers almost half of South America and is the only country there where Portuguese is the main language.

questions.question: Which direction does a compass needle point to?
questions.fact: A compass points to magnetic north, which isn't exactly the North Pole and slowly wanders over time.

questions.question: How many weeks are there in a year?
questions.fact: 52 weeks is only 364 days, which is why your birthday falls one weekday later each year (two after a leap day).

questions.question: Which gemstone is red?
questions.fact: Rubies and sapphires are the same mineral, corundum. Red ones are rubies; every other colour is a sapphire.

questions.question: Which gemstone is green?
questions.fact: Emeralds are a green form of the mineral beryl. Colombia is famous for some of the finest emeralds in the world.

questions.question: What is the traditional gift for a 25th wedding anniversary?
questions.fact: A 25th anniversary is the silver wedding. The custom comes from old German traditions of giving a silver wreath.

questions.question: What is the traditional gift for a 50th wedding anniversary?
questions.fact: After gold (50) comes diamond (60). Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip even reached platinum, 70 years, in 2017.

questions.question: What is the traditional gift for a first wedding anniversary?
questions.fact: The second anniversary is traditionally cotton and the fifth is wood. Paper comes first, fragile like a brand-new marriage.

questions.question: On which hand is the wedding ring traditionally worn in Spain?
options: It is worn on a necklace
questions.fact: In Spain, Germany and much of Eastern Europe the wedding ring goes on the right hand. In the UK and US it goes on the left.

questions.question: How many items are in a dozen?
questions.fact: Twelve is handy for trading because it divides evenly by 2, 3, 4 and 6. Ten only divides by 2 and 5.

questions.question: How many items are in a "gross"?
questions.fact: A gross is a dozen dozens (12 × 12). A "great gross" is a dozen gross: 1,728.

questions.question: How many is a "score"?
questions.fact: Abraham Lincoln's Gettysburg Address begins "Four score and seven years ago", which means 87 years.

questions.question: What is the currency of the United Kingdom?
questions.fact: The pound sterling is said to be the oldest currency still in use, with a history of over 1,200 years.

questions.question: What is the currency of Switzerland?
questions.fact: The Swiss franc's code is CHF, from "Confoederatio Helvetica", the Latin name of Switzerland.

questions.question: What is 7 times 8?
questions.fact: A handy rhyme: "5, 6, 7, 8 — 56 is 7 times 8."

questions.question: Which is the smallest continent?
questions.fact: Australia is the only continent that is also a single country. It's often grouped with nearby islands as "Oceania".

questions.question: How many minutes are in an hour and a half?
questions.fact: 90 minutes is also the length of a football match: two halves of 45 minutes.

questions.question: How many seconds are in an hour?
questions.fact: With 3,600 seconds in an hour, a day has 86,400 seconds.

questions.question: How many sides does a pentagon have?
questions.fact: The Pentagon in the USA, one of the world's largest office buildings, has five sides and five floors above ground.

questions.question: Which day comes two days after Friday?
questions.fact: Saturday is named after the Roman god Saturn, and Sunday after the Sun.

questions.question: Which month comes right after July?
questions.fact: August is named after Augustus, the first Roman emperor. July is named after Julius Caesar.

questions.question: How many legs do three dogs have altogether?
questions.fact: Three dogs, 12 legs. Bonus fact: dogs sweat mainly through the pads of their paws.

questions.question: In which season do leaves fall from most trees?
questions.fact: Leaves turn colour in autumn because trees stop making green chlorophyll, revealing yellows and oranges that were there all along.

questions.question: What do you call someone who designs buildings?
questions.fact: The word "architect" comes from Greek and means "chief builder".

questions.question: At Rome's Trevi Fountain, how should you throw a coin for good luck?
options: Over your right shoulder with your left hand
Over your left shoulder with your right hand
questions.fact: Legend says one coin means you'll return to Rome. Over a million euros a year is fished out of the fountain and given to charity.

questions.question: Which is heavier: a kilo of feathers or a kilo of iron?
questions.fact: A kilo is a kilo! But a kilo of feathers takes up far more space, which is why the trick catches people out.

questions.question: How many months have 28 days?
questions.fact: Every month has at least 28 days. February is the only one with fewer than 30.

questions.question: What has keys but can't open locks?
questions.fact: A piano is a string instrument and a percussion instrument at once: little hammers strike the strings.

questions.question: What gets wetter the more it dries?
questions.fact: Towels dry you by soaking the water up themselves. The little loops on a terry towel give it more surface to hold water.
